pairs.why: Both locomotives have the same near-black body against a bright desert and sky, and neither differs from the other in key, value groups or vignette.

A keeps the sand small and the water deeper and more uniform, so the dark post and ring group stands out more, as in the real card's dark water. B puts a bright sand and foam band in the foreground, which pulls the lightest value away from the hero.
B has a larger hero and mid-teal stripes with softer separation, which matches the real card's gentle mid-key stripes better than A's glaring bright cyan.

A has a saturated mid-dark background that darkens toward the corners and a strong light glow behind a dark boot, like the real cards' vignetted backgrounds. B is a pale, washed, high-key sky blue with a mid-value boot and little corner darkening.
A has a slightly deeper purple wall and a more solid, saturated orange glass that separates clearly from the background. B's glass is paler and hazier.
A has a soft glow behind the hero and gentle local contrast, like the real card. B has deeper, harder darks at the corners and in the hero shading.
B has dark cuffs and dark grey blades against yellow on a mid purple background, which matches the real card's value groups. A has a bright magenta glow and cuffs that blend into the background.
Both are bright, evenly lit scenes with similar dark green and brown accents, and neither reproduces the real card's dark vignette and dark lower shelf.
